correctness.rationale: The frozen RESULT.md proof was reconstructed. For a simple Steiner S(2,k,v) with r=(v−1)/(k−1) and b=vr/k, a chosen block B0 containing all t<=k marked points splits points into named singletons, U=B0−marks, W=V−B0 and blocks into B0, A_i through individual marked points, A_U meeting U, A_W disjoint from B0. Pair uniqueness implies every block !=B0 meets B0 at most once. Each W vertex meets one off-B0 block through each of k points on B0 and r−k disjoint blocks; every degree between cells and every cell size is parameter-only. This common equitable template proves all-order C2 indistinguishability for any designs of the same parameters. For a noncollinear STS triple, the pair block of two named anchors is definable by a C2 rank-one formula, its third point by rank two, and existence of one block through the three completion points has rank four. The completions are distinct by noncollinearity; the sentence is exactly Pasch. Independent finite enumeration from separately written code produced PG(3,2): 35 lines, 35 collinear and 420 noncollinear triples, all 420 Pasch-completing (105 four-block Pasch configurations); Bose Z5×Z3: 35 lines, 35 collinear, 420 noncollinear and 0 Pasch-completing. Independent joint 1-WL verified all mark choices t=0,1,2 for both systems and all 35 collinear lines per system match for seven rounds; every one of 420 noncollinear triples on each side matches rounds 0,1,2 against a fixed opposite witness, and separates at round 3, yielding qrank lower bound 4 for the pair. These exhaustive finite checks apply ONLY to the two order-15 witnesses; the universal theorem follows from the symbolic cell table.
residual_risks: All-size C2 inference relies on standard correspondence of stable colour refinement with two-variable counting logic, proved in cited primary literature.
Seven refinement rounds are not proof of complete equivalence; the symbolic equitable partition supplies that proof.
Rank four optimality is for the displayed two order-15 systems with noncollinear marked triples, not for arbitrary STS.
The source proof assumes noncollinear marks for the Pasch formula; collinear marks are handled separately by equitable blindness.

The coarsest equitable partition theorem and biregular-replacement lemmas of Kiefer–Schweitzer–Selman and Arvind–Köbler–Rattan–Verbitsky are prior foundations. They do not state or, without explicit design-specific incidence accounting, fix the blockwise named-marker C2 theory. Prior anti-Pasch literature supplies (or potentially supplies) the Bose witness and STS15 Pasch-free census, but not the pairwise first distinction at three noncollinear marks with quantifier depth exactly four. All 4 named comparisons were conducted by implications and matching objects. Originality is qualified: specialized earlier work could contain an equivalent calculation, and relevant anti-Pasch full text was inaccessible.

value.rationale: Pasch is the canonical smallest nontrivial six-point four-block Steiner configuration, and landmark individualization in C2/1-WL is a natural expressive-power invariant for incidence graphs. For any nontrivial Steiner 2-design the all-size theorem proves parameter-only indistinguishability even after separately naming all points of a complete block, while moving from two to three noncollinear anchor points permits a concrete rank-four Pasch witness. The 15-point PG/Bose pair demonstrates both a true landmark cutoff and a strict minimum logical depth, not just unrelated counts. Neither the finite examples nor the known C2 correspondence alone implies this sharp joint structural statement. Its precise scale and dependence on collinearity are mathematically motivated, and no paper-sized generalization is required.
residual_risks: Value attaches to the exact landmark-complexity threshold and all-design blockwise theorem, not claimed first discovery of Bose anti-Pasch order-15 systems.
No classification of arbitrary noncollinear markings or higher-dimensional WL is provided.

limitations: Universal theorem proved symbolically only for 0..k named collinear points of nontrivial simple Steiner 2-(v,k,1) designs, not arbitrary marked configurations.
